thread:
erin: Heads-up — new contributor hit a horrible import error when following the quickstart. `from redwood import AsyncClient` fails only when dev installed via pipx/poetry, wheels are fine.

mike: Oof. Can you paste the error + how they installed?

erin: Error after the quickstart steps: `pipx runpip poetry install --dev --no-root` then `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"` -> `ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'redwood'`. They were using pipx to run poetry to avoid polluting global env.

houston: That's an unusual combo. Pipx isolates installs into venvs; mixing that with poetry's editable/develop mode can confuse import resolution. Did they use PEP 660 editable wheels or legacy egg-link flow?

erm: (typo) erin: I think their pip / poetry versions are older (pip 22, poetry 1.2). So no PEP 660 support.

mike: When PEP 660 isn't supported, editable installs rely on path-based metadata that expects distribution name == package dir. What's our distribution name in pyproject?

erin: pyproject has `name = "redwood-inference"` but package dir is `redwood/` in source. No explicit packages declared.

houston: Bingo. Wheels will bake correct package metadata, but editable metadata (egg-link / develop) can drop the mapping or expose the distribution name mismatch. Pipx/v1 also rewrites site-packages paths which can make it worse.

ci-bot: CI alert: reproducible failure in editable-smoke job #8242. Artifact: https://ci.example/8242/artifacts — shows missing `py.typed` and dist-name mismatch.

mike: Additional wrinkle: our test suite imports `redwood_async` in some places (old/legacy) which masked the issue in CI vs local. Also some consumers pin `httpx==0.22.*` in their lockfiles causing runtime attribute errors in AsyncClient during debugging.

erin: Workarounds posted to the contributor: (1) use a wheel: `python -m build && pip install dist/*.whl` (2) upgrade pip/poetry to support PEP 660 (pip >= 23, poetry plug-in or newer poetry) (3) avoid pipx for dev flow for now.

houston: Long-term fixes: (a) in pyproject add explicit packages mapping (e.g., `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["."]` or `packages = ["redwood"]`), (b) include `py.typed` in package data if we ship typing stubs, (c) optionally make distribution name match top-level package (e.g., `name = "redwood"`) or add `dynamic = ["name"]` — weigh the brand vs packaging ergonomics.

mike: Also propose a contributor guide update in repo root: section "Local dev install" showing recommended `python -m pip install -e .` and wheel-based install, and mention pip/poetry/pipx version matrix. I'll draft.

docs: I'll add a short paragraph in the Quickstart that says: "For local development, build a wheel and pip install it, or use poetry with PEP 660-capable pip. Avoid pipx for running poetry during install."

erin: Can we add a CI smoke test that does an editable install (both `pip install -e .` and `poetry install --develop`) and runs `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient"`? That would've caught this earlier.

ci-bot: Noted. Ticket created on infra board: validate editable install in PR checks and surface packaging metadata errors. Linked CI job: https://ci.example/infra/2491

mike: I'll open SDK GH issue with reproduction steps, minimal pyproject diff, and proposed CI test. Will tag eng-runtime and contributor experience.

erin: Filed issue #1310: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/issues/1310 — attached repro and suggested fix.

houston: TL;DR for engineers: editable installs can be fragile across toolchains (pipx + older pip/poetry). Ensure packaging metadata explicitly maps distribution -> package, include py.typed, and add editable-install smoke test.

erin: Thanks — shared the fix in the contributor PR and updated the quickstart. New contributor confirmed they can run the sample app after installing wheel. :rocket:
